key: No, here thou diest not, thou art not injured: by easy paths unto the Gods thou goest.
s: Near the end of a hymn on the horse sacrifice, the horse, now killed, is addressed; Sāyaṇa, on 1.162.21, takes the killing as no death like other horses’ and no pointless harm, answering the objection that the death is seen: the horse reaches the gods.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.162.21, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 401046 (2024)

evidence.words: नैव इदानीम् इतराश्ववत् मृतो भवसि देवत्वप्राप्तेर्वक्ष्यमाणत्वात्। अत एव “न “रिष्यसि न हिंस्यसे । व्यर्थहिंसायाः अभावात् । ननु प्रत्यक्ष्यतो मृतिः अवयवनाशश्च दृश्यते कथमेवमुच्यते इति । उच्यते। … देवानेव प्राप्नोषि। अतो युक्तैषोक्तिः।
evidence.gloss: You surely do not now die as other horses die, since your reaching godhood is about to be stated; for that very reason you are not harmed, not injured, since there is no pointless injury. But surely death and the destruction of the limbs are seen before the eyes: how can this be said? It is answered: ... you reach the gods themselves. So the statement is fitting.
